phoropter: one command, run inside a repository, that indexes, builds and serves

Today phoropter is three invocations you have to know: node src/build.ts <repo> [commit], node src/serve.ts <repo> [commit] --port …, and nothing at all for keeping indexes, which are rebuilt from scratch every time. This plan makes it one command, phoropter, that you run inside a repository. It's the first of the plans toward a phoropter CLI. Plugins for indexers and UIs, and how phoropter is installed, come after.

It takes in the index store worked out with Jeff and shelved as shelf/index-store.md. That plan couldn't land alone: its writing half was phoropter index, a command this plan makes. Two plans that only work together are a distributed transaction, so they're one plan now. Its decisions are restated here as Jeff answered them, and the seed is deleted when this converts.

Decision: phoropter with no arguments serves the repository you're in

where src/serve.ts file page

quote // node src/serve.ts <repo> [commit] [--out site] [--port 4173]

Because (Claude, not asked): the person reading plans is standing in the repository. phoropter finds its root by walking up to .git, indexes what's missing into the local cache, builds the site at HEAD, and serves it with the draft and notes in drafts/, as the dev server does now. It prints the address. phoropter <path> does the same for another repository, and --at <commit> serves another commit. Outside a git repository, it says it reads one and stops. This is the experience the whole CLI is for: "you run ph in the repo" (Jeff). Every other command is secondary to it.

For now it opens nothing; it prints the address. Jeff thinks a UI is the right default, with the address shown so it can be handed to the agent, and that closing the UI could stop the server. Both depend on what "a UI" is, so they're the plugin plan's to decide, and they're written into its seed (shelf/ui-plugins.md). This plan is whole without them: a server and its address are a complete thing. A later plan that opens a UI adds to it and leaves nothing broken here.

Decision: The port is 4173, or the next free one

where src/build.ts file page

quote options: { out: { type: 'string', default: 'site' }, port: { type: 'string', default: '4173' } },

Because (Claude, measured): this pair already serves two repositories at once (mock-control on 4173, phoropter on 4175), and choosing a port by hand each time is friction. If 4173 is taken, phoropter takes the next free port and prints it. --port still pins one.

Decision: phoropter url says where the server is, for the agent and the UI

where (new) src/cli.ts file page

made by the work, so there is nothing to resolve

Because (Jeff, then Claude): "the address displayed somewhere so it can be handed to the agent. Is there a better way to do that?" Taking the next free port means nobody can guess the address anymore, and that gap would be this plan's own. So while it serves, phoropter records the address, the repository's root, the commit and its process in a small file outside the repository, under the cache directory, keyed by the root. It removes the file when it stops. phoropter url, run anywhere in the repository, prints the address of the server for it, or says none is running. CLAUDE.md can tell an agent to run it, and a UI can show it. Writing outside the repository keeps phoropter a reader of it.

Decision: A repository with no plans gets a welcome, not an error

where src/render.ts file page

quote <p>No plans in <code>plans/</code> at this commit.</p>

Because (Jeff): "what if there are no plans?" It's how every repository starts. The site still builds: the home page says there are no plans yet, links the guide's first section ("Write the plan"), and says where a draft would go. The guide is served on every site already (twill). Phoropter doesn't create plans/ or a first draft: that's init, and phoropter only reads. Jeff's idea for init is that the first draft is about how the pair works together, with the defaults as its prompts' fallbacks ("the agent always asks before converting a plan to code", defaulting to no). It's in init's seed. init is a write, so it belongs to the UI side. When it exists, the welcome page points to it. Until then the welcome is whole on its own.

Decision: phoropter build writes the static site, as build.ts does

where src/build.ts file page

quote // node src/build.ts <repo> [commit] [--out site]

Because (gimlet): a static site generator plus a dev server, not a running API. The built site stays a function of one commit, for publishing or reading from file://, and never holds a draft or notes. phoropter build takes the same <path>, --at and --out, and uses the same index store, so a second build of the same commit doesn't re-index.

Decision: Indexes are facts about commits, stored apart from pages

where shelf/index-store.md file page

quote # Seed: indexes are facts about commits, kept apart from pages

Because (Jeff and Claude, from the index store): three layers. Plans are testimony, committed and never edited. Indexes are facts about commits that never change. Pages are a cheap projection of the two, never committed. Gimlet's reasons not to commit the site hold, and two more came up: a committed site is always one commit behind, and the "now" column changes nearly every page on every commit. The expensive, fragile part was never the pages. It's indexing old commits, whose toolchains may be gone.

  • Each index is stored per commit, package, and indexer with its version, and never changes. Phoropter keeps only what it reads (each definition's symbol, file and line range), as JSON, not the raw .scip. Measured on mock-control at f02528f: 185 definitions from about 970 lines of TypeScript make 29.7 KB of JSON, 2.5 KB compressed as git stores it, indexed in under half a second. That's about 30 bytes of JSON per line of source. The file leaves out its commit (the path has it) and sorts its keys, so a package that didn't change between two plan commits gives byte-identical files, which git stores once.
  • The indexes plans need are committed, in .phoropter/index/<sha>/<package>.json, like a lockfile. That way a plan's symbol anchors outlive their toolchain. Per branch is safe: keyed by sha, merges only add directories, and an index survives a squash merge that loses its commit. A cache outside the repository and git notes were weighed and set aside (Jeff).
  • The index for now lives in a local cache, $XDG_CACHE_HOME/phoropter/ or ~/.cache/phoropter/, under the same key. It moves with every commit, so committing it would be the churn gimlet avoided.
  • A build indexes only what's missing, from the store and then the cache (Jeff: "index the missing pieces"). The draft, re-read on every request, reads the same store, so a refresh doesn't wait on an indexer.
  • A missing indexer is a view status, no-index, naming the indexer it needed, and never a failed build. The profile defines it.

Decision: phoropter index is the one command that writes into the repository

where src/scip.ts file page

quote export function indexCommit(repo: Repo, sha: string, packages: Set<string>): Map<string, Definition> {

Because (Jeff): a build never writes into the repository it reads. Loden says "Phoropter only reads", and gimlet made the site "never a place to write." phoropter index writes the indexes plan commits need into .phoropter/index/, from the cache or by indexing, because a person ran it to do exactly that. It writes nothing else, and git shows the new files to commit. A build that found plan commits only in the cache says so, and names the command ("safest for now", Jeff).

Decision: package.json names the command, and the npm scripts stay

where package.json file page

quote "dev": "node src/serve.ts ../mock-control 90c65b9",

Because (Claude, not asked): a bin entry makes phoropter a command in this repository (npx phoropter) and anywhere after npm link, since Node 24 runs the .ts sources directly. How phoropter is installed for other people is the shipping plan's question. npm run dev stays as it is, serving mock-control at an old commit for the tests and for Jeff's habit.

Decline: Opening a UI or a browser, in this plan

Because (Claude, not asked): what to open is a choice between UIs, and UIs as plugins is the next plan, with Jeff's ideas for it in its seed. Until then, the address is printed, and phoropter url finds it again.

Decline: Watching the repository and rebuilding as commits land

Because (Claude, not asked): the site is a function of one commit (gimlet), and the working tree's draft and notes are already re-read on every request. A new commit is a new phoropter. A watcher may earn a plan once there's a reason, not before.

Guess: Someone new to a repository is reading its plans within a minute of phoropter

Answered in the as-built: held.

Disproved if: on a fresh clone of mock-control or this repository, with the committed index store in place, phoropter takes more than a minute to print its address, or prints anything that has to be read twice.
